newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Vanstone says on track for budget forecasts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Vanstone says on track for budget forecasts.

text.p: Australian Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone said on Thursday the government was on track to meet its budget forecasts for unemployment and employment for the 1996/97 (July-June) year.
"We are on target for our budget projections and I am very pleased with that," Vanstone told reporters when asked about employment growth and the unemployment rate.
The government has forecast average employment growth for the year to June 30, 1997 of 1.5 percent and an unemployment rate of 8.25 percent at June 30, 1997.
Figures released earlier on Thursday showed unemployment rose to 8.8 percent in February from 8.6 percent in January and employment fell 7,200 in February.
Vanstone said the labour market was very flat in February.
"The pleasing news is that trend employment...is now at its highest level and in trend terms, the unemployment rate has remained stable at 8.6," she said.
Vanstone said trend unemployment was much more reliable than the volatile seasonally adjusted series.
Asked about the trend to part-time employment, Vanstone said this had been evident for some years.
"I believe that is a reflection of the resistance of employers to taking people on full-time," she said.
"They are taking people on on a part-time and casual basis because they want the flexibility that provides."
The government had introduced structural changes to the industrial relations system, but these would take some time to flow through.
"In the meantime, I would expect employers to take on people on a part-time and casual basis to give them flexibility," she said.
In February, full-time employment fell 24,200, while part-time employment rose 17,000.
